items.prompt: I want to understand gene regulation during zebrafish fin regeneration: five time points, four replicates each, bulk RNA-seq. Any thoughts on how to approach it?

Last time GIRAFFE on our 52 prostate samples didn't seem to converge, so this time please use a learning rate of 0.001, 500 iterations and a stronger weight on the PPI term. Same expression, motif and PPI files as before.

Kick off PANDA with expr_kidney.tsv (it has a header row, so with_header on), motif_kidney.tsv and ppi_kidney.tsv, and use cobra_out/adjusted_coexpression.tsv from yesterday's COBRA run as the co-expression input instead of plain Pearson. Save the network as panda_kidney_adjusted.txt now.

Please use LIONESS-OTTER on our 64 asthma airway samples so each patient gets their own OTTER network. We have expression, a motif seed and a TF-TF PPI ready, and we specifically want OTTER's graph matching per patient, not PANDA.
I uploaded hcc_expr.tsv, hcc_motif.tsv, hcc_ppi.tsv and hcc_mirna.txt for 33 liver tumours. Go ahead and run the analysis; we'll work out afterwards what question it answers.
Here are expr_pdac.tsv, motif_hs.tsv and ppi_hs.tsv. Run PANDA or GIRAFFE on them now, whichever; I just need something to show at lab meeting on Thursday.

Each of my pig muscle samples should get its own gene-gene co-expression network (log2 CPM, centered per gene). We have three samples, unless the degraded one gets excluded, in which case only two. I won't know until Monday.

Can DRAGON give me a single partial-correlation network across transcriptomics, proteomics and metabolomics together? All three tables come from the same 75 patients, samples as rows. I want all three layers in one model rather than separate pairwise runs.

Using liver_expr.tsv, liver_motif.tsv and liver_ppi.tsv for our 44 donors, start the per-donor analysis now. I need one number per TF per donor for a survival model, but I haven't settled whether that number should be the TF's activity or its out-degree in the donor's own network.

I'd like DRAGON on two tables from the same 85 plasma donors: proteomics (310 proteins, log-intensities) and metabolomics (140 metabolites, log-abundances), samples as rows and features as columns. Please fix lambda1 at 0 and lambda2 at 1 rather than estimating them, and give me the edge_list output so I can sort the cross-layer partial correlations.

Please start LIONESS-DRAGON now with layer 1 = rna_top400.csv (100 samples by the 400 most variable genes, log-CPM) and layer 2 = meth_top200.csv (the same 100 sample IDs by 200 CpG M-values). Leave lambda1 and lambda2 empty so they're estimated, and write dragon_all.tsv and lioness_dragon_samples.tsv.
PANDA or OTTER: which one should I use for my 50 lung adenocarcinoma samples? I have the expression matrix, a human motif prior and a STRING PPI file ready to go.

Go ahead and run LIONESS-PUMA: expression expr_ovarian.tsv (48 tumours, genes by samples), prior motif_tf_mirna.tsv (TF motifs plus miRNA targets), ppi_string.tsv and mirna_ids.txt with one miRNA per line. Aggregate network to out/puma_aggregate.txt and the per-sample networks to out/lioness_puma/.

LIONESS-DRAGON for 40 paired RNA and miRNA profiles from the same placentas would be ideal. The miRNA layer has 300 features, but I can't remember whether we kept 450 or 4,500 genes in the RNA layer after filtering.

For 55 endometrial tumours I want each miRNA's activity level in every tumour, estimated apart from the miRNA's own expression; the same idea as transcription factor activity, but with miRNAs as the regulators.
I have RNA-seq from 36 mouse livers, half on a high-fat diet and half on chow. What kind of network analysis should I be doing with this?

Please set up SAMBAR for somatic mutation calls from 8 pancreatic tumours, with a gene-length table, a cancer-gene list and a KEGG pathway GMT that is not in MSigDB format, so turn gmt_msigdb off. Try kmin 3 up to kmax 8, and keep the normalization by each patient's mutation burden.
Our panel has somatic mutation calls and RNA-seq for the same 150 colorectal patients, plus survival data. What could NetZoo do for us with data like this? We're open to anything.

We have paired proteome (250 proteins) and phosphoproteome (150 sites) tables from 46 kidney tumours and want a partial-correlation network linking the two layers. The aims page says one network for the whole cohort, the grant narrative says one per tumour, and I can't tell which my PI meant.

Launch LIONESS-DRAGON on rna_all.csv (60 samples by 2,000 genes) and prot_all.csv (the same 60 samples by 500 proteins). Estimate the lambdas automatically, write the all-sample matrix to agg_dragon.tsv and the per-sample table to per_sample_edges.tsv, and start it right away.

Execute OTTER on expr_heart.tsv, motif_heart.tsv and ppi_heart.tsv right now and save otter_heart.tsv. My notebook says lam should be 1.5, or maybe 0.15; the decimal point is smudged and I can't check with my supervisor today.

We want to group tumours into 2 to 6 subtypes based on pathway-level somatic mutation scores, with gene lengths, a cancer-gene list and a KEGG GMT in hand. Pathology review is still deciding how many tumours qualify: it will end up as 5 or 9.
My lab keeps telling me to 'do LIONESS' on our 200 TCGA breast tumour RNA-seq profiles. Is that something I should be doing, and what would I get out of it?

For 40 glioblastoma samples I want one cohort-wide regulatory network in which both transcription factors and miRNAs regulate their target genes. I have the expression matrix, a prior with TF motifs and miRNA target predictions, a PPI file and a list of the miRNAs, one per line. Per-sample networks aren't needed.

Please launch something on expr_tpm.tsv (48 gut biopsies, genes by samples) and batch_design.tsv (numeric batch and site columns). Not sure yet what I'm after, maybe something co-expression related? Whatever you think fits.

We measured proteomics and metabolomics on the same 90 plasma samples (continuous, log-scaled), and reviewers asked for 'a systems-level angle'. We don't have a specific hypothesis yet. Where would you start?

COBRA seems right for separating sex and batch effects on co-expression in our 640-sample blood cohort; the design matrix is numeric. The README says the filtered expression matrix has 600 genes, but the methods draft says 6,000, and I honestly don't know which is right.

We have 18,000 genes measured in 96 colon samples from three hospitals and two sequencing batches, with a numeric design matrix (one-hot hospital, batch, age) keyed by the same sample IDs. I want to see how much of the gene co-expression is associated with hospital and batch, and get an adjusted co-expression matrix out of it.
Start a run on rna_layer.csv and protein_layer.csv (same 64 samples, continuous values, about 300 features each). DRAGON or LIONESS-DRAGON, your call; I need results by Friday.

I need a separate gene-gene co-expression network for each of 30 bulk RNA-seq samples of human skin (log2 CPM, centered per gene, genes on rows). There are no covariates to adjust and no transcription factors involved, just one co-expression network per sample.

From matched liver RNA-seq and metabolomics on 70 mice, I need a network that proves which metabolites causally drive which genes, with arrows showing the direction of each effect, to support a mechanistic claim in our paper.
Is GIRAFFE worth trying on my melanoma data? I have expression for 70 tumours plus motif and PPI files. I'm hoping something interesting falls out of it.

I have just two RNA-seq samples from one patient, tumour and matched normal, and want a separate TF-to-gene regulatory network for each of the two, built from motif and PPI priors, so I can compare them edge by edge.

I've put calls_30pts.csv, gene_lengths.csv, cancer_genes.txt and kegg.gmt in data/; start SAMBAR into sambar_30/ now. No one documented the old pipeline that made calls_30pts.csv, so it's unclear to me whether it holds somatic mutations or germline variants.

Our seven tumours are in mut_7tumours.csv. Together with exon_lengths.csv, cancer_genes.txt and c2.cp.v7.gmt, please execute SAMBAR now into sambar_out/ with kmin 2 and kmax 10, so we see a wide range of subtype numbers.

Our cervical cancer project (38 samples) needs one regulatory network for the whole cohort, with TFs and a set of small RNAs as regulators of the genes. A collaborator sent the small-RNA list and target predictions, but nobody can tell me whether those small RNAs are miRNAs or piRNAs.

BONOBO run please, right away: expr_lc.tsv (12 lung samples, log-transformed and centered), sparsify on at confidence 0.05, .h5 output in bonobo_lc/. Set delta to 0.5, or was it 0.2? I can't remember what my postdoc suggested.
Someone in journal club suggested BONOBO, someone else said COBRA, for our 24 bladder cancer RNA-seq samples with batch information. Which one do I go with?

Can we use DRAGON on our gut study: a host transcriptome table (log CPM) and a metabolite table for the same 58 stool samples? One thing I can't vouch for: the metabolite file may hold actual intensities or just 0/1 detected/not-detected calls.

Run CONDOR now on results/panda_lung_edges.tsv: columns source, target and weight, thresholded from my PANDA lung network so all weights are non-negative. Write everything into /data/projects/lung/condor_results/ and use lung_v1 as the prefix.

Our downstream pipeline only reads parquet, so BONOBO should write each per-sample co-expression matrix for our 22 lung fibroblast samples as a .parquet file. The expression is log-transformed and centered, with genes on rows.

We profiled a targeted panel of 400 immune genes in 650 blood samples and have a numeric design matrix with age, sex and batch. The goal is the co-expression attributable to each covariate plus a batch-adjusted co-expression matrix.

Across 120 breast tumours I need, for each transcription factor, its activity level in every tumour separately from its own mRNA level, and also whether it activates or represses each target gene. I have RNA-seq expression, a TF-gene motif prior and a TF-TF PPI matrix with matching identifiers.

Time to rerun OTTER: expr_pbmc.tsv, motif_pbmc.tsv and ppi_pbmc.tsv, output otter_pbmc.tsv as an edge list. This time set computing to gpu and precision to single, because the CPU run took far too long on our 19,000-gene matrix. Start it now.

We only have three bulk RNA-seq samples of mouse retina (P7, P14 and adult), plus a mouse motif prior and a STRING PPI. I know it's a tiny set, but I'd like LIONESS-PANDA to give each of the three samples its own TF-to-gene network, kept separate from the aggregate one.
Please run CONDOR directly on expr_tpm_brain.tsv (genes by 40 cortex samples) to find gene communities, and write the output to condor_brain/ today. We don't want any network-building step first.

Could you set up OTTER for an aggregate TF-gene network of human cardiomyocytes, using my precomputed gene-by-gene co-expression matrix instead of an expression table, plus the motif seed and the TF-TF PPI? Settings: lam = 1, gamma = 0, 150 iterations, single precision on CPU, matrix output.

I want LIONESS-PANDA networks for our zebrafish heart regeneration study, one per fish. After QC we kept either two or four libraries; the sequencing core still hasn't told me which. We have the zebrafish motif prior and PPI.
